text:
maya: Heads up — noticed Karpenter launched a weird mix of GPU instance types in us-west-2 this morning and ended up with AZ skew + eni IP pressure. pods stuck Pending for ~12m. anyone else see this? :thinking:

jon: I saw that too. looks like it preferred g4dn.xlarge in az-a even though load was spread. some pods got scheduled then failed on CNI attach.

devon: can you paste the provisioner yaml + the pod tolerations? my guess: consolidation rules + mixed-instance policy triggered cross-AZ packing and broke our ENI budget assumption.

maya: here's the provisioner snippet we use (trimmed):
```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: kubernetes.io/arch
      operator: In
      values: [amd64]
  provider:
    instanceProfile: redwood-provisioner-role
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: us-west-2
  consolidation: true
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 30
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: 1000
      nvidia.com/gpu: 120
  providerRef: {}
```

alex: curious about `subnetSelector` — are you targeting a small set of subnets per AZ? that can force cross-AZ launches if capacity/spot options differ. also what are your instance type preferences?

maya: we set `nodeSelector` for gpu workloads and left instance types open but have `labels` that prefer p4/p3/g4 families. we also have a warm-pool in az-a for fast startup.

lee: the pattern I observed: when eviction/drain happened on old nodes, karpenter created new heterogeneous nodes in az-a because warm-pool + spot price signals. then many pods with hostNetwork false still needed ENIs, and the trunking quota for az-a hit 80% -> CNI attach fails.

jon: can we mitigate with two changes: 1) tighten instance type requirements so Karpenter doesn't mix high-eni-per-host and low-eni ones in same AZ, 2) adjust consolidation to avoid packing pods that will increase ENI usage?

devon: +1. also consider `ttlSecondsUntilExpired` for warm pools so warm nodes don't persist and lure scheduling into one AZ. and maybe explicit `topologySpreadConstraints` on daemonset-like gpu consumers to force AZ distribution.

maya: quick repro logs: `kubelet` shows `AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume` and `Failed to allocate IP from trunk` around the same timestamps.

alex: I whipped a small policy suggestion: force instanceClass preference grouped by `eniCapacity` label. Example provider `requirements` change: 
```
- key: redwood.com/eni-capacity
  operator: In
  values: [high, medium]
```
then have two provisioners: one for high-eni hosts and one for medium. avoids mixed packing.

lee: that would be more explicit. downside: more provisioners to manage but it's safer for now.

jon: Another operational short-term: lower `consolidation` to false during business hours for GPU heavy clusters, run consolidation in a nightly window. keeps latency predictable.

maya: sounds reasonable. can someone draft a PR with: - split provisioners (high/medium eni) - set `ttlSecondsAfterEmpty` for warm-pools to 300s - add `topologySpreadConstraints` for gpu pods

devon: I'll take the PR. will also add a small e2e in staging to simulate ENI exhaustion (scale runners + drain).

sre-bot: [alert] 1855003000 - ENI quota in us-west-2a at 82% for account redwood-prod, automated paging escalated to oncall.

maya: thanks — if the PR lands today let's also bump the autoscaler fallback to dedicated on capacity shortages (fallback route) so user traffic doesn't hit degraded inference.

jon: noted. will coordinate with product infra to enable fallback policy.

lee: one more long-term item: can we get telemetry from instances about theoretical ENI capacity per instance type into model selection so Karpenter can prefer types that fit our CNI envelope?

devon: filing infra-ops ticket for that integration after PR.

maya: perfect. I'll post the PR link here when it's up. :thumbsup:
